_comment: What counts as an account that can actually be tagged, stated once (#926).
Read by tests/test_real_handle.py and
PostRollApp/Tests/RealHandleTests.swift, which drive
postroll.caption_blocks.is_real_handle and PythonBridge.isRealHandle.
Those two are the pair that spans the bridge on the deliverable: Python's
week_tags calls one and Swift's weekTags reaches the other through
TypedCredit.read, and what they let through is the TAG LIST Dan pastes
into Instagram's Tag people field.
Two questions, both of which have to pass, and neither answers the other
(L118). SHAPED like a username, which tests/fixtures/handle_shape.json
states on its own: 'DPR Dance' is a real company and no account. And not a
SENTINEL, one of the words recorded because somebody looked and found no
Instagram: 'unknown' is perfectly well shaped and nobody at all.
The sentinels are listed here rather than only in code because each side
keeps its own copy, caption_blocks.HANDLE_SENTINELS and
PythonBridge.handleSentinels, maintained by hand beside each other (L41).
Both tests assert their side's set is exactly this one, so a word added to
either alone is reported rather than found later in a caption.
A blacklist admits every placeholder nobody thought to list (L257). That is
what ships on both sides today, and widening it to a real account check is
a separate change; what this file exists to stop is the two sides widening
differently.
The sentinel has to be read AFTER the value is stripped down to a bare
username, not before. Python did and Swift did not, so a sentinel arriving
as a pasted profile link or behind a second sigil was refused by Python and
accepted by Swift, which then handed 'unknown' to the tag list as an
account. Those cases are marked below.

cases.why: the account the reported caption should have carried
the @ is stripped before either half is read
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, not content
a pasted profile link names an account somebody can act on
a dot inside a handle is legal
underscores are legal
Instagram is case insensitive but the case is not an error
digits are legal, including first
starts with the sentinel 'no' and is its own account, so the sentinel is matched whole and never as a prefix
the same for 'skip', because a real handle can begin with any of these words
the same for 'na', on the other side of the boundary
a sentinel: somebody looked and there is no Instagram
a sentinel, and the slash makes it badly shaped as well
a sentinel
a sentinel
a sentinel, written as a dash in the handle book
a sentinel
a sentinel
the sentinel is read case insensitively
and after the value is trimmed
a sigil in front of a sentinel does not make it an account
every leading sigil is stripped before the sentinel is read; Swift stripped one and accepted this
a sentinel pasted as a profile link is still a sentinel; Swift read the whole URL against the list, missed, and put 'unknown' in the tag list
the reported defect: a company's display name typed into the handle field
any space at all, whatever the case
two accounts inside a sentence, stored in the org book today
a person's name, with a comma and a trailing dot
a dot never ends a handle, because a full stop looks the same
Instagram has no hyphens in usernames
nothing is not an account
whitespace alone is not an account
the sigil with no name behind it
every leading sigil is stripped, leaving nothing
a link to Instagram itself names no account
a character Instagram does not allow
accented letters are outside the allowed set
